patients.summary: Administrative assistant who joins in 2020 with obesity and recurrent UTIs on nitrofurantoin prophylaxis. PCOS, hidradenitis and IBS are diagnosed by outside specialists in 2022; gallstones lead to cholangitis, ERCP with sphincterotomy for sphincter of Oddi dysfunction and cholecystectomy in 2024. documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient. 26 y/o woman moving her care here; prior PCP office closing its adult panel. Records requested.

Concerns today: none acute. Wants a regular doctor and help with weight.

PMH: recurrent bladder infections since about age 23, at least three a year, cultures at the old office per pt. Prior PCP put her on nightly nitrofurantoin and she has had none since starting it. Acne as a teen and in her early 20s, used prescription creams, nothing now. Weight has been her biggest frustration.
PSH: none.
Meds: nitrofurantoin 100 mg at bedtime.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: mother with type 2 diabetes and gallstones; father with high blood pressure; one sister with polycystic ovaries.
SH: administrative assistant. Smokes cigarettes daily, has tried to stop before. No alcohol. Lives locally.

ROS: negative except as above. No dysuria now.

Exam: well appearing, NAD. Vitals as recorded; BMI 36. HEENT normal. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without rash. Ext warm, no edema. Mood and affect appropriate. PHQ-9: 3.

A/P:
1. Obesity, BMI 36. Talked about realistic targets, food log, walking at lunch. Recheck weight in a year or sooner.
2. Tobacco use. Advised to quit; she is not ready to set a date but open to revisiting. Offered support whenever she wants it.
3. Hx recurrent UTI on prophylaxis. Doing well on nitrofurantoin, will continue and refill here.
4. Health maintenance: Tdap today (no record of one since high school). Baseline CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, TSH. One-time HIV and hep C screening, she agrees. Pap 2019 at prior office, normal per pt; will confirm with records. Flu shot when this season's supply comes in.

RTC 1 year for physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: obstetrics and gynecology
documents.body:
Gynecology consultation, seen 04/18/2022. Referred by primary care.

Thank you for sending Ms. Harris, 28, for irregular cycles and difficulty conceiving. Menses come roughly every two to three months and are often heavy and prolonged. She has been trying to conceive for a year without success. Over about two years she has seen more hair on the face and abdomen. She denies thyroid symptoms and galactorrhea.

Medications: nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA. Former smoker, stopped a year ago when they began trying. No alcohol. Family: mother with type 2 diabetes and gallstones, sister with PCOS, father with hypertension.

Exam: BMI 32. Darkened velvety skin at the back and sides of the neck consistent with acanthosis nigricans. Mild terminal hair on the upper lip and chin. Remainder unremarkable.

Results: fasting glucose 98 mg/dL. Total testosterone 82 ng/dL (reference 15-70). Prolactin 14 ng/mL. TSH 2.1. Lipids within normal limits. Pelvic ultrasound shows numerous small peripheral follicles in both ovaries.

Impression: polycystic ovary syndrome, with oligo-ovulation, clinical and biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Insulin resistance suggested by the acanthosis.

Plan: start metformin, increasing to 1000 mg twice daily with meals over a few weeks as tolerated. Continue the prenatal vitamin. Continue weight efforts. Will follow in clinic.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

Dermatology new patient consultation
Date of service: 06/13/2022
Reason for referral: recurrent painful nodules

History: 28-year-old woman with recently diagnosed PCOS who reports recurring painful nodules and abscesses in both axillae and the groin, with spots that drain and reform along tracts. Meds: metformin, nitrofurantoin, prenatal vitamin. NKDA. Former smoker.

Examination: bilateral axillae with several inflamed nodules, two interconnected sinus tracts, and rope-like scarring. Inguinal folds with recurrent nodules and a single sinus tract on the right, with areas of normal skin between lesions. A few comedones and papules on the jawline.

Assessment: hidradenitis suppurativa, Hurley stage II. Mild acne.

Plan: clindamycin 1% gel to affected areas twice daily, which will also cover the jawline. Loose cotton clothing, avoid shaving over active lesions. Weight loss helps. Return in about 6 to 9 months.

GASTROENTEROLOGY - NEW PATIENT
Visit date: 10/03/2022

Referral question: recurrent abdominal pain with change in bowel habit.

HPI: 28-year-old with PCOS (seen by gynecology) and hidradenitis (seen by dermatology). For roughly six months she has had abdominal pain more than weekly, commonly brought on by meals and relieved by defecation, with alternating stretches of diarrhea and constipation. No recent travel, no ill contacts, no antibiotic courses apart from long-standing low-dose nitrofurantoin. No rectal bleeding or nocturnal stools.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, topical clindamycin. NKDA.
Family history: noncontributory.
Social: former smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: abdomen soft and not distended, no tenderness, no masses, bowel sounds normal.

Labs today: Hgb 11.2 g/dL, MCV 86 fL, WBC 7.0. CRP 2 mg/L, ESR 15 mm/hr.

Impression: irritable bowel syndrome, mixed subtype, by Rome IV criteria. Normal inflammatory markers are reassuring.

Recommendations: dicyclomine 10 mg up to three times a day as needed for cramping. Dietary fiber and a low-FODMAP trial with handout. Follow up here as needed.

Gastroenterology

Dermatology return visit - 04/06/2023

Known to our practice for hidradenitis suppurativa since June 2022, with polycystic ovary syndrome diagnosed by gynecology in April 2022. Today her main concern is gradual thinning over the crown during the past year. She describes cycles every 35 to 60 days and finds weight hard to shift even with regular exercise and careful eating. Past acne treated with topicals. Using clindamycin gel for HS.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, nitrofurantoin 100 mg daily, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, clindamycin 1% gel BID. NKDA.

BP 125/78. BMI 32. Diffuse widening of the central part over the vertex with preserved frontal hairline; no scarring, no scale. Coarse terminal hair on the chin, upper lip and sideburn area in a male-type distribution. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Axillary HS quiet today.

Labs: fasting glucose 96 mg/dL; total testosterone 82 ng/dL (reference 8-60); TSH 2.5; lipids normal.

Assessment: thinning at the crown and hirsutism, both consistent with the androgen excess of her known PCOS. Thyroid normal. HS stable on topical therapy.

Plan: continue current topical regimen for HS. Gentle hair care, avoid tight styles. Coordinate hormonal management with gynecology. Return in one year or sooner for flares.

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 04/04/2024 21:40

Chief complaint: right upper abdominal pain.

HPI: 30 yo F with PCOS, hidradenitis (Hurley II), IBS and history of recurrent UTIs, followed for her IBS and HS, here with 5 hours of severe, waxing and waning RUQ pain that bores through to her back, starting after a big dinner. Nauseated, has not vomited. Bowel movements unchanged, urine normal color.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, nitrofurantoin 100 mg qhs, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, clindamycin gel. Allergies: NKDA. Former smoker, no EtOH.

Exam: vital signs stable, afebrile. Uncomfortable, shifting on the stretcher. Abdomen: marked RUQ tenderness, no rebound, no guarding; positive Murphy's sign. Lungs clear, heart regular.

Labs: Hgb 12.5, WBC 10.0. T bili 1.2, alk phos 120, AST 40, ALT 45. Amylase 90, lipase 45. Urine hCG negative.

Imaging: RUQ US with multiple gallstones, no cholecystitis.

ED course: IV ketorolac and IV ondansetron with relief; tolerated PO.

Impression: symptomatic cholelithiasis (biliary colic).

Disposition: discharged home. Ondansetron ODT 4 mg q8h prn. Low-fat diet. Follow up with PCP this week to arrange general surgery evaluation; return for fever, jaundice or pain lasting more than a few hours.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/04/2024 from the ED. Discharged 10/08/2024.

Principal diagnosis: acute cholangitis.
Secondary: cholelithiasis; sphincter of Oddi dysfunction (papillary stenosis) s/p biliary sphincterotomy; PCOS; hidradenitis suppurativa; IBS; obesity.

Hospital course: admitted febrile and jaundiced with a dilated common duct. Treated with IV fluids and piperacillin-tazobactam. Blood cultures without growth. ERCP 10/05: cannulation of a tight, stenotic papilla; cholangiogram showed a dilated common bile duct with sludge and several small stones, cleared with balloon sweeps after biliary sphincterotomy. Endoscopist's impression was papillary stenosis (sphincter of Oddi dysfunction) with choledocholithiasis. No post-procedure pancreatitis. Defervesced within 24 hours, pain resolved, diet advanced. Bilirubin 1.3 and alk phos 141 on 10/07.

Discharge medications: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID for 5 more days. Resume metformin, nitrofurantoin, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, topical clindamycin.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week. General surgery for interval laparoscopic cholecystectomy in about 4-6 weeks; referral sent from inpatient team.

Allergies: NKDA.

Hospital Medicine

- Gallstones, cholecystectomy pending - keep the 10/28 surgery appt.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT - 11/18/2024
Preoperative diagnosis: symptomatic cholelithiasis, status post cholangitis and ERCP sphincterotomy.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.

Findings: gallbladder as expected. Critical view of safety obtained. Cystic duct and artery clipped and divided. Gallbladder removed from the liver bed and extracted in a bag through the umbilical port.
EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same day, tolerating diet. Acetaminophen as needed; no opioids requested.
Pathology: chronic cholecystitis with cholelithiasis.
Follow-up in surgery clinic in 2 weeks.

OBSTETRICS - PRENATAL VISIT, 10/06/2025
GA 10w0d by LMP 7/28/25, consistent with dating scan. EDD 5/4/2026.

Known to us for PCOS with long-standing subfertility. Here for routine prenatal care; no complaints, pregnancy uneventful so far. No dysuria, frequency or flank pain.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, nitrofurantoin 100 mg daily, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, topical clindamycin. NKDA.
PMH also notable for hidradenitis, IBS, cholangitis 2024 with ERCP sphincterotomy and cholecystectomy, recurrent UTIs.
Former smoker, no alcohol.

BP 120/78, HR 72, T 37.0 C. Exam unremarkable.

Urinalysis: leukocyte esterase 1+, nitrite positive, 20-29 WBC/hpf. Culture: E. coli >100,000 CFU/mL.

Assessment: intrauterine pregnancy at 10 weeks. Asymptomatic bacteriuria.
Plan: amoxicillin 500 mg TID x 7 days. Repeat urine culture two weeks after finishing. Continue current medications. Return in 4 weeks.

events.reason: Fatigue, poor appetite and dark urine in pregnancy

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PROVIDER NOTE, 01/16/2026

CC: tired, not eating, dark urine.

32-year-old G1 at 24w4d with history of sphincter of Oddi dysfunction and cholangitis in 2024 (sphincterotomy, then cholecystectomy). About a week of fatigue and poor appetite, and her urine has turned dark. No prior liver disease, no alcohol, no drugs, no recent travel, no sick contacts. First-trimester prenatal screening was unremarkable.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, dicyclomine prn, clindamycin gel. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile, vitals within normal limits. Scleral icterus. Mild RUQ tenderness. No rash. Gravid abdomen appropriate for dates. Remainder normal.

Labs: total bilirubin 3.2, direct 1.5, AST 850, ALT 920, alk phos 210, total protein 7.1, albumin 4.0. PT 12 sec (control 11). WBC 5.0, Hgb 12.1, platelets 210.

MDM: marked hepatocellular injury in pregnancy with preserved synthetic function. Hepatitis serologies sent. OB evaluated in the ED: fetal heart tones normal. Patient stable for discharge with close hepatology follow-up arranged for next week; return for confusion, bleeding, vomiting, abdominal pain or decreased fetal movement.

documents.title: Hepatology Consultation
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
HEPATOLOGY CONSULTATION - 01/23/2026
Referred from the ED.

32-year-old at 25 weeks with acute hepatocellular injury found 1/16 (AST 850, ALT 920, bilirubin 3.2). Prior biliary history: cholangitis 2024 treated by ERCP sphincterotomy for papillary stenosis, then cholecystectomy. Has taken nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly for UTI prophylaxis continuously for about eight years. No alcohol, supplements other than the prenatal vitamin, or new medicines. Feels somewhat better, urine lighter.

Exam: mild scleral icterus, abdomen gravid and nontender, no stigmata of chronic liver disease.

Serologies from 1/16: hepatitis A IgM, hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis B core IgM and hepatitis C antibody all nonreactive.
Today: AST 312, ALT 405, alk phos 182, total bilirubin 1.6.

Impression: toxic liver disease - drug-induced hepatocellular injury, most likely from long-term nitrofurantoin. Viral hepatitis excluded by serology; already improving.

Plan: stop nitrofurantoin now and do not rechallenge. Do not restart for prophylaxis. Repeat hepatic panel in four weeks. OB aware.

Hepatology follow-up, 02/20/2026, 29 weeks pregnant.

Off nitrofurantoin since 1/23. Energy and appetite back, urine normal color, no itching.

AST 44, ALT 61, alk phos 150 (placental contribution expected), total bilirubin 0.8.

Impression: nitrofurantoin-associated liver injury, resolving.
Plan: OB to repeat a hepatic panel at delivery admission. No further hepatology visits needed unless that is abnormal. Avoid nitrofurantoin in future; please add to her intolerance list.

OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/01/2026 in spontaneous labor at 39w4d. Discharged 05/03/2026.

Antepartum course: PCOS on metformin. Asymptomatic bacteriuria at 10 weeks, treated, test of cure negative. Drug-induced liver injury at 24 weeks attributed to nitrofurantoin, which was stopped; resolved by 29 weeks. Tdap given in the third trimester.

Admission labs: hepatic panel and CBC within normal limits.

Delivery: uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery on 05/01/2026 of a healthy infant. Mother and baby recovered routinely.

Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin, metformin 1000 mg BID, acetaminophen as needed.
Intolerance: nitrofurantoin (liver injury).
Follow-up: postpartum visit with OB in 6 weeks; PCP for ongoing care.
